title: Excel-based Employee Management System (Full Scope)
description:
## Problem Statement

The user has an interview take-home exercise: given an Excel file of employee data (ID, Name, Department, Salary, Join Date, Status, Last Updated Date) and a short requirements document, they must build a web application that lists, searches/filters, and CRUDs this data. Beyond the bare requirement, the user wants their submission to demonstrate broader engineering maturity — AI integration, import/export support, and readiness to run against multiple database backends — and wants the underlying system design, architecture, infrastructure, and deployment story to hold up under interview-level scrutiny on security, performance, scalability, and maintainability, including a live on-the-spot feature-addition challenge.

## Solution

A full-stack Employee Management system split across three repositories:

- A **backend** repo (.NET 9, Clean-Architecture-lite: Domain / Application / Infrastructure / Api / McpServer projects in one solution) exposing a REST API and, in-process, an MCP server over stdio that mirrors the same use-cases for AI-client consumption.
- A **frontend** repo (Vite + React, feature-based folder structure, TanStack Router + TanStack Query, Zustand, shadcn/ui + Tailwind, an OpenAPI-generated typed API client).
- An **infra** repo holding only a `docker-compose.yml` that pulls prebuilt backend/frontend images from a container registry alongside PostgreSQL, for a one-command full-stack local demo.

The system manages Employee and Department records with full CRUD, search/filtering, Excel/CSV import/export, JWT-based authentication with Admin/Viewer roles, an automatic audit trail, and a database layer that is provider-swappable (SQLite for local dev, PostgreSQL via Docker) through configuration alone.

## User Stories

1. As an HR administrator, I want to see a paginated list of all employees, so that I can review headcount data without loading the entire dataset at once.
2. As an HR administrator, I want to search employees by name, so that I can quickly find a specific person.
3. As an HR administrator, I want to filter employees by Department, so that I can see everyone in a specific team.
4. As an HR administrator, I want to filter employees by Status (Active/In Active), so that I can distinguish current staff from former staff.
5. As an HR administrator, I want to filter employees by a Salary range, so that I can analyze compensation bands.
6. As an HR administrator, I want to filter employees by a Join Date range, so that I can review hiring activity over a period.
7. As an HR administrator, I want to combine multiple filters at once, so that I can narrow down to exactly the records I need.
8. As an HR administrator, I want my current filter to be reflected in the URL, so that I can bookmark or share a specific view.
9. As an HR administrator, I want to add a new employee via a form, so that new hires are recorded in the system.
10. As an HR administrator, I want the employee ID auto-generated on create, so that I never manage unique identifiers manually.
11. As an HR administrator, I want to pick Department from a dropdown of existing active departments, so that I don't introduce typos or duplicate names.
12. As an HR administrator, I want Salary displayed and entered with `#,##0.00` formatting, so that figures are easy to read and consistent.
13. As an HR administrator, I want to pick Join Date from a calendar/date input, so that dates are always valid and consistently formatted.
14. As an HR administrator, I want to toggle Status with a single checkbox, so that updating employment status is a one-click action.
15. As an HR administrator, I want Last Updated Date stamped automatically whenever a record changes, so that I always know how fresh the data is without manual entry.
16. As an HR administrator, I want to edit an existing employee's details, so that I can correct or update their record.
17. As an HR administrator, I want to delete an employee record after confirming, so that I can remove entries that no longer belong, without doing so by accident.
18. As an HR administrator, I want field-level validation errors shown next to the relevant form field, so that I know exactly what to fix.
19. As an HR administrator, I want a dedicated screen to manage Departments (add, rename, disable), so that the dropdown reflects the organization's real structure over time.
20. As an HR administrator, I want a disabled Department to disappear from the dropdown for new records but remain valid on existing ones, so that historical data stays intact.
21. As a Viewer-role user, I want to list and search employees, so that I can look up information without being able to change it.
22. As an Admin-role user, I want exclusive access to create/update/delete on Employees and Departments, so that data changes are controlled.
23. As any user, I want to log in and stay signed in via short-lived access tokens that refresh silently, so that I don't get logged out mid-task but a stolen token has a short shelf life.
24. As an unauthenticated visitor, I want to be redirected to a login page when I try to access the app, so that data is never exposed without credentials.
25. As an Admin, I want every create/update/delete on Employee or Department recorded with who/when/what changed, so that I have an audit trail for sensitive HR/salary data.
26. As an Admin, I want to view the audit log filtered by entity type or date, so that I can investigate a specific change.
27. As an Admin, I want to export the current filtered employee list to Excel or CSV, so that I can share or archive a snapshot outside the app.
28. As an Admin, I want to import an Excel file of employees, so that I can bulk-load or bulk-update data instead of entering it one by one.
29. As an Admin, I want an invalid import file rejected in its entirety with a row-by-row error report, so that I never end up with a silently incomplete or partially-applied dataset, and I know exactly which rows to fix.
30. As an AI coding assistant (MCP client), I want to call the same list/search/create/update/delete operations as MCP tools, so that I can manage employee data on the user's behalf during a demo or live session.
31. As a developer extending this app, I want the persistence layer written against a provider-agnostic abstraction, so that switching from SQLite to PostgreSQL requires configuration only, not code changes.
32. As a developer/interviewer, I want the whole stack runnable locally via `docker-compose up` against prebuilt images, so that the "production-shaped" deployment story is demonstrable, not just described.
33. As a developer, I want each repository's CI to build, test, and only then publish a container image, so that a broken build can never produce a deployable artifact.
34. As a developer, I want unit and integration tests at the API boundary (real HTTP pipeline, real SQLite) covering business rules, so that both the REST surface and the MCP tools that share the same use-cases are proven correct by one seam.
35. As a developer, I want frontend feature tests that mock only the network boundary (not hooks or store internals), so that tests exercise real component + data-fetching + form wiring.
36. As a developer preparing for a live coding challenge, I want a consistent architectural pattern for adding a field, a filter, or an MCP tool, so that an on-the-spot feature request can be implemented quickly and correctly under time pressure.

## Implementation Decisions

- **Repository layout**: three repositories — `backend` (.NET 9 solution containing Domain, Application, Infrastructure, Api, and McpServer projects), `frontend` (Vite + React), and `infra` (compose-only, no source code).
- **Backend architecture**: Clean-Architecture-lite. A single Application layer of use-case services holds all business logic; the REST API and the MCP server are both thin adapters over the same in-process Application layer (the MCP server is a project within the backend solution, referencing Application directly — not a separate deployable calling the REST API over HTTP).
- **Data model**: `Employee` (Id, Name, DepartmentId FK, Salary, JoinDate, IsActive, UpdatedAt — IsActive is a boolean internally, mapped to "Active"/"In Active" text only at the Excel/CSV I/O boundary); `Department` (Id, Name, IsActive — soft-disable, never hard-deleted, so historical Employee references stay valid); `AuditLog` (EntityName, EntityId, Action, ChangedBy, ChangedAt, ChangesJson), populated by a single shared EF Core `SaveChanges` interceptor that also stamps `UpdatedAt`.
- **Database**: EF Core against a provider selected via configuration — SQLite as the local-dev default, PostgreSQL as the alternate provider (via Docker), switched purely through config, no code change and no simultaneous multi-source connections.
- **Search/Filter**: server-side, translated to EF Core queries — never client-side filtering of a fully loaded dataset. Supports Name (partial match), Department, Status, Salary range, Join Date range, all combinable, reflected in the frontend router's URL state.
- **Authentication & Authorization**: JWT access token + refresh token, both delivered as httpOnly cookies; a refresh endpoint rotates them. Two roles: Admin (full CRUD, import/export, audit log access) and Viewer (read/search only). Write endpoints enforce Admin; read endpoints require any authenticated session.
- **Import/Export**: Excel (.xlsx) and CSV, both directions. Import validates every row against the same rules as manual entry (Name required, Department must exist and be active, Salary numeric, Join Date valid) before writing anything; any invalid row rolls back the entire import atomically, but the response carries a full row-by-row error report (row number, field, reason) rather than a generic failure. Export honors the currently applied filter.
- **MCP Server**: hosted in-process within the backend solution over stdio transport, tools mirror the Application-layer use-cases (list/search/get/create/update/delete Employee, list/manage Department, import/export). No separate authentication on the MCP boundary — it shares the same-machine trust boundary as the process it's part of.
- **Frontend architecture**: feature-based (vertical slice) folder structure — one folder per capability (employees, departments, auth), each self-contained with its own components/hooks/api calls/types, plus shared `ui` (shadcn primitives) and `lib` (API client, utilities). Routing via TanStack Router. Server state via TanStack Query. Client-only state (current user/role, UI state) via Zustand. Forms via React Hook Form + Zod. API types generated from the backend's OpenAPI/Swagger spec rather than hand-written.
- **CI/CD**: each of the backend and frontend repos runs its own independent CI pipeline — build, run its test suite, and only on green build/push a Docker image to GitHub Container Registry. The `infra` repo's compose file references those published image tags; it never builds from source.
- **Deployment target**: local demonstration only, via the `infra` repo's `docker-compose up`. No live cloud hosting is part of this spec — a cloud deployment is a talking point built on the same published images, not a deliverable.
- **Git workflow**: trunk-based — direct commits to `main` in each repository; no PR ceremony for this solo build.
- **Live-coding-challenge readiness**: no specific feature is pre-guessed or pre-built for the live challenge; instead, the shared Application-layer pattern (one seam for both REST and MCP, one validation/EF Core migration pattern) is kept consistent enough that adding a field, a filter, or an MCP tool follows one repeatable, fast path.

## Testing Decisions

- A good test asserts observable behavior (HTTP response status/body, or rendered UI state) — never internal implementation details such as which private method or component internal was called.
- **Backend seam (primary, single)**: the HTTP API boundary, exercised via `WebApplicationFactory<Program>` against a real SQLite (in-memory/temp-file) database. This is the one seam that proves both the REST controllers and, indirectly, the Application-layer use-cases the MCP tools also call.
- **MCP adapter check (secondary, thin)**: because MCP tools are thin wrappers over the same Application-layer use-cases already proven at the backend seam, MCP gets only a smoke test confirming each registered tool dispatches to the correct use-case and returns the expected result shape — business rules are not re-tested here.
- **Frontend seam (primary, single)**: feature/page-level render tests (React Testing Library) with the network mocked at the HTTP boundary (MSW) rather than mocking hooks, TanStack Query internals, or the Zustand store directly — tests exercise real component + query + form wiring end to end.
- No manual API-client tooling (e.g. Bruno) is part of the test suite — the integration-test seam above is considered sufficient coverage of the API surface.
- No prior art exists in this repo yet (greenfield project); these two seams establish the testing pattern for all future work here.

## Out of Scope

- Any manual/black-box API testing tool (e.g. Bruno) — deliberately dropped in favor of the WebApplicationFactory integration-test seam.
- Live deployment to any cloud provider — the deliverable is a local `docker-compose up` demo plus the CI-built images, not a hosted environment.
- A feature-branch/PR workflow — this solo build uses trunk-based commits directly to `main`.
- Automated end-to-end (browser) tests (e.g. Playwright) — frontend testing stops at the feature/page render-test seam.
- Simultaneous/federated connections to more than one database at a time — "multi-database support" means a config-driven single-provider switch (SQLite ⇄ PostgreSQL), not cross-database querying.
- An HTTP/SSE transport for the MCP server — stdio only.
- Any in-app AI chat/assistant UI — the MCP server is the entire "AI Integration" deliverable, not a supplementary chat feature.
- Hard-deleting Departments — only soft-disable is supported.

## Further Notes

- This spec is the parent of the 11 tracer-bullet tickets already published in Beads (Walking Skeleton, Employee CRUD, Department Master Data, Search & Filter, Authentication & RBAC, Audit Log, Import/Export, MCP Server, Multi-Database Verification, CI Pipelines, Infra Repo Compose Orchestration) — those tickets carry the acceptance criteria and blocking-edge sequencing; this document is the shared context behind them.
- An earlier, unrelated Beads epic (`excel-management-liw`) from a separate session was found and deleted at the user's explicit request during this session, because it described a materially smaller scope (two projects, no auth, no multi-repo, HTTP-transport MCP, Bruno included) built against a stated interview deadline of 2026-09-14 17:00–18:00. That deadline note has not been independently reconfirmed in this session — if it is still real, the scope in this spec (three repos, full RBAC, audit logging, CI/CD publishing to a registry, Postgres verification) is substantially larger than what a single-evening interview-prep window can realistically complete, and the priority order in a time crunch should be: (1) Walking Skeleton + Employee CRUD + Department + Search/Filter, (2) Auth + Import/Export, (3) MCP Server, (4) Audit Log + CI/CD + Multi-DB + Infra compose — cut from the bottom of that list first, not the top.

title: Walking Skeleton — Employee List end-to-end
description:
## What to build

Scaffold both repos and prove the full stack is wired together end to end with one real, demoable slice: a paginated Employee list.

Backend: Clean Architecture project layout (Domain / Application / Infrastructure / Api / McpServer project stubs) inside a single .NET solution. EF Core DbContext for Employee and Department entities matching the fields from the source Excel data (Employee: Id, Name, DepartmentId, Salary, JoinDate, IsActive, UpdatedAt; Department: Id, Name, IsActive), with the connection provider selectable via config (SQLite by default, Postgres-ready). Seed the sample rows from the source Excel data. Expose one paginated `GET /employees` endpoint.

Frontend: Vite + React app scaffold using the agreed feature-based folder structure, TanStack Router, TanStack Query, Zustand, shadcn/ui + Tailwind, and an OpenAPI-generated typed API client. Render the employee list page against the real endpoint.

This ticket proves the wiring (API ↔ DB ↔ Frontend), not business rules — those come in later tickets.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Backend solution builds with Domain/Application/Infrastructure/Api/McpServer projects present (McpServer can be an empty stub for now)
- [ ] EF Core migration creates Employee + Department tables against SQLite; the same migration applies cleanly if pointed at a Postgres connection string
- [ ] Sample data from the source Excel file is seeded on first run
- [ ] `GET /employees` returns paginated results
- [ ] Frontend app scaffold renders the employee list page fetching from the real endpoint, using the agreed frontend stack (TanStack Router/Query, Zustand, shadcn/ui+Tailwind, generated API client)
- [ ] Backend integration test (WebApplicationFactory + SQLite in-memory) covers `GET /employees`
- [ ] Frontend render test (RTL + MSW) covers the list page rendering seeded data

## Blocked by

None — can start immediately.
close_reason: Walking skeleton done: Clean Architecture .NET solution + EF Core (Sqlite/Postgres-swappable) seeded from source Excel data, paginated GET /employees; Vite/React frontend (TanStack Router/Query, Zustand, shadcn/ui+Tailwind, generated OpenAPI client) rendering it. Backend integration test + frontend RTL/MSW test green, verified live in a browser end-to-end. Code-reviewed (Standards+Spec axes); fixes applied. Postgres migration compatibility explicitly deferred to excel-management-8ui (notes added there).

title: MCP Server — AI Tool Access
description:
## What to build

An MCP server, running as its own process within the backend solution (stdio transport), that exposes the same Employee/Department capabilities to an AI client (e.g. Claude Desktop/Code) as tools: list/search employees, get employee by id, create/update/delete employee, list departments, and get an employee-data export. Tools call directly into the existing Application-layer use-cases in-process — no HTTP hop, no duplicated business logic, no separate auth (same-machine stdio trust boundary, consistent with the earlier design decision).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] MCP server process starts and registers one tool per use-case listed above
- [ ] Each tool's input/output shape is documented (tool description) well enough for an AI client to call it correctly without guessing
- [ ] Each tool delegates to the same Application-layer use-case the REST API uses — no reimplemented validation or business logic
- [ ] A smoke test invokes each registered tool directly and asserts it dispatches to the correct use-case and returns the expected result shape (business rules themselves are covered by ticket 2/3's tests, not re-tested here)
- [ ] A manual walkthrough confirms an AI client (e.g. Claude Desktop) can list, create, and update an employee through the MCP server

## Blocked by

2 — Employee CRUD
3 — Department Master Data Management
close_reason: MCP server implemented via ModelContextProtocol SDK; 7 tools delegating to existing Application-layer repositories; 12 smoke tests + full suite green after merge

title: Import / Export (Excel + CSV)
description:
## What to build

Admin-only bulk data movement in and out of the system via Excel and CSV.

Export produces a file (Excel or CSV) of the currently filtered Employee list, using the same fields and formatting conventions as the source data (e.g. Status as Active/In Active text, not a raw boolean).

Import accepts an Excel file, validates every row against the same rules as ticket 2 (Name required, Department must exist and be active, Salary numeric, Join Date valid) plus row-level referential checks. Validation runs against the whole file before anything is written: if any row fails, nothing is committed (atomic, all-or-nothing), and the response is a row-by-row error report (row number, field, reason) so the user can fix the file and re-upload — not a single generic failure message.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Export endpoint produces a valid Excel file and a valid CSV file for the currently filtered Employee list, with Status rendered as Active/In Active text
- [ ] Import endpoint accepts an Excel file and validates every row before committing anything
- [ ] A file with one or more invalid rows commits nothing and returns a row-by-row error report (row number, field, reason) covering every failing row, not just the first
- [ ] A fully valid file commits all rows in a single transaction
- [ ] Import/export endpoints are Admin-only; a Viewer-role request is rejected (403)
- [ ] Backend integration tests cover: valid file import, file with mixed valid/invalid rows (asserting nothing was committed and the full error report), and export round-trip

## Blocked by

2 — Employee CRUD
3 — Department Master Data Management
5 — Authentication & RBAC
close_reason: Added Admin-only Employee Import/Export (Excel + CSV). Export: GET /employees/export?format=excel|csv reuses the existing filter query, new unpaged IEmployeeRepository.GetAllAsync (extracted shared filter-building from GetPagedAsync). Status rendered as Active/In Active text in both formats. Import: POST /employees/import (multipart file), validates every row via ClosedXML parsing + reuses EmployeeValidator for Name/Salary/JoinDate/Department rules (Department matched by name against active departments), collects full row-by-row error report, all-or-nothing via single SaveChangesAsync. 7 new integration tests (valid import, mixed valid/invalid commits nothing + full error report, export excel/csv, export round-trip, viewer 403) - 53/53 backend tests green. Frontend: Export Excel/CSV + Import buttons with row-error table on EmployeeListPage, admin-gated; OpenAPI client regenerated; tsc clean; 10/10 frontend tests green. Tradeoff: import matches department by name (case-insensitive) not ID, for round-trip friendliness with the exported file - documented in code.

title: Audit Log
description:
## What to build

An audit trail of every create/update/delete on Employee and Department: who changed it, when, what action, and what changed — captured automatically by a single shared persistence-layer mechanism (not sprinkled per endpoint), and viewable by an Admin.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every create/update/delete on Employee or Department writes one audit entry (entity name, entity id, action, changed-by user, timestamp, and a representation of what changed)
- [ ] The audit-writing mechanism is a single shared piece of infrastructure, not duplicated per endpoint/use-case
- [ ] An Admin-only screen lists audit entries with basic filtering (by entity type and/or date range)
- [ ] A Viewer-role request to the audit screen/endpoint is rejected (403)
- [ ] Backend integration test confirms an audit entry is created for a create, an update, and a delete, and that Viewer access is rejected

## Blocked by

2 — Employee CRUD
5 — Authentication & RBAC
close_reason: Built AuditLog domain entity (EntityName/EntityId/Action enum/ChangedBy/Timestamp/Changes-as-JSON) + IAuditLogRepository/AuditLogRepository + GET /audit-logs (AdminOnly, filters by entityName/from/to). Single shared write path: AppDbContext.SaveChangesAsync/SaveChanges override inspects ChangeTracker for Employee/Department Added/Modified/Deleted -- no changes to EmployeeRepository/DepartmentRepository/endpoints. Real bug found+fixed via live Postgres spot-check: a naive one-pass 'add audit rows before base.SaveChangesAsync' captured EF's temporary placeholder key values for Created rows (Id and any FK to a same-batch-new parent showed garbage negative sentinels, reproduced via seed data). Fixed with a two-phase save under one transaction: Updated/Deleted diffs captured pre-save (original values reset after save), entity save runs first to resolve generated keys, then Created diffs/EntityId are read from the now-resolved entry and the audit rows are saved. Migration: scaffolded against the Postgres provider (not the Sqlite default) because the frozen model snapshot was already Postgres-shaped from a prior migration -- scaffolding under Sqlite reverted all existing Users/Employees/Departments columns to Sqlite types in the same migration (destructive, confirmed by EF's own data-loss warning). Verified end-to-end: 54/54 backend tests green (7 new AuditLogTests: create/update/delete each produce exactly one entry, viewer gets 403, unauthenticated gets 401, entity/date filtering), migration applied cleanly to a real Postgres 17 container (Docker) from a fresh DB, and a manual create/update/delete cycle against it confirmed correct types (character varying, integer identity, timestamptz) and correct audit content. Frontend: admin-gated /audit-log route + AuditLogPage (entity-type + date-range filters), nav link added next to Departments; tsc -b clean, existing suite 10/10 green. Tradeoff: audit list has no pagination (ticket only asked for filtering; matches the Department list's precedent) -- add if log volume grows large enough to matter.

title: Authentication & RBAC (Admin/Viewer)
description:
## What to build

Login flow and role-based access control with two roles: Admin (full CRUD) and Viewer (list/search/read only).

Backend issues a JWT access token plus a refresh token on login, both delivered as httpOnly cookies; a refresh endpoint rotates them. Every write endpoint (create/update/delete on Employee and Department) requires the Admin role; read/list/search endpoints require any authenticated user. The frontend redirects unauthenticated users to a login page, hides/disables write actions (add/edit/delete buttons) for Viewer-role users, and holds the current user/role in the agreed client-side store.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Login endpoint issues an access token + refresh token as httpOnly cookies for a valid credential; rejects invalid ones
- [ ] Refresh endpoint rotates the access token using a valid refresh token
- [ ] Write endpoints (Employee/Department create/update/delete) return 403 for a Viewer-role token and succeed for an Admin-role token
- [ ] Read endpoints succeed for both roles; return 401 with no/invalid token
- [ ] Frontend redirects an unauthenticated user to the login page when visiting a protected route
- [ ] Frontend hides or disables create/edit/delete controls for a Viewer-role session
- [ ] Backend integration tests cover login, refresh, and the 401/403 cases above
- [ ] Frontend render test covers the unauthenticated redirect and the Viewer-role UI restriction

## Blocked by

1 — Walking Skeleton
close_reason: Implemented JWT cookie auth + Admin/Viewer RBAC; 32 backend + 9 frontend tests green; live-verified in browser; follow-up ujs.2 filed for refresh-token revocation gap

title: Search & Filter
description:
## What to build

Server-side search and filtering across the Employee list, replacing the skeleton's plain pagination with real query capability: filter by Name (partial match), Department, Status (active/inactive), a Salary range, and a Join Date range. Filters compose together (AND) and are reflected in the URL so a filtered view is shareable/bookmarkable.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `GET /employees` accepts query parameters for name search, department, status, salary range, and join-date range, all combinable
- [ ] Filter panel UI exposes all of the above and updates the list without a full page reload
- [ ] Current filter state is reflected in the URL (via the router) so reloading the page preserves the filter
- [ ] Backend integration tests cover at least one single-filter case and one combined-filter case
- [ ] Frontend render test covers applying a filter and seeing the list update accordingly

## Blocked by

2 — Employee CRUD
3 — Department Master Data Management
close_reason: Server-side search/filter (name/department/status/salary-range/join-date-range, AND-composed) with URL-reflected filter panel; 47 backend + 10 frontend tests green; live-verified combined filtering in browser; fixed a real per-keystroke loading-flash bug and a history-spam bug found during review

title: Department Master Data Management
description:
## What to build

Full CRUD screen for Department as its own master-data entity, so the Employee form's department dropdown becomes editable data rather than fixed seed rows.

Departments can be renamed and soft-disabled (`IsActive = false`) rather than hard-deleted, so historical Employee records that reference a disabled department still display correctly. A disabled department drops out of the dropdown for new/edited Employee records but remains valid for existing ones.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `GET/POST/PUT /departments` endpoints support listing, creating, renaming, and toggling `IsActive`
- [ ] Department is never hard-deleted through the UI, only soft-disabled
- [ ] Department admin screen lists all departments (including disabled ones) and lets an admin toggle/rename them
- [ ] The Employee create/edit dropdown only offers active departments, but an existing Employee referencing a disabled department still renders and saves correctly
- [ ] Backend integration tests cover create/rename/disable and the "existing reference to a disabled department still valid" case
- [ ] Frontend render tests cover the department admin screen and the filtered dropdown behavior

## Blocked by

1 — Walking Skeleton
close_reason: Department Master Data done: GET/POST/PUT /departments (active-only by default, includeInactive=true for admin), soft-disable only (never hard-deleted), name required+unique validation. Admin screen lists all incl. disabled with inline rename+toggle. Employee dropdown offers active only but still renders/saves an existing reference to a disabled department correctly (fixed a real Base UI Select label-resolution bug found via live testing: form now waits for departments to load before mounting). 18 backend integration tests + 7 frontend RTL/MSW tests, all green. Code-reviewed (Standards+Spec); fixed a state-staleness bug where toggling Active could silently persist an unsaved rename. Filed excel-management-ujs.1 (P4) for a minor check-then-act race on name uniqueness — not blocking. Verified live end-to-end in a browser (disable HR, confirm it drops from create dropdown but Charlie Day's existing HR reference still shows/saves).

title: Employee CRUD (Create/Update/Delete)
description:
## What to build

Full create/update/delete flow for an Employee, end to end, on top of the walking skeleton's list/read path.

Validation follows the field rules from the source Excel's Requirement sheet: Name is required free text, Department must reference an existing Department, Salary is a non-negative number, Join Date is a valid date, Status is a checkbox (stored internally as a boolean, displayed as Active/In Active). Last Updated Date is stamped automatically on every write, not user-editable.

Delete requires a confirmation step. Validation errors from the API are surfaced next to the relevant form field in the UI, not just as a generic error banner.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `POST/PUT/DELETE /employees` endpoints implement create/update/delete with the validation rules above
- [ ] Create/Edit form (React Hook Form + Zod) mirrors the same validation rules client-side
- [ ] Delete requires an explicit confirmation step in the UI
- [ ] Field-level validation errors from the API are shown next to the relevant form field
- [ ] `UpdatedAt` is set automatically by the backend on every write and is never accepted from client input
- [ ] Backend integration tests cover create/update/delete including at least one validation failure per rule
- [ ] Frontend render tests cover the create and edit form flows, including a validation error case

## Blocked by

1 — Walking Skeleton
close_reason: Employee CRUD done: POST/PUT/DELETE /employees + GET /employees/{id}, GET /departments (prefactor for 9n4). Validation (Name required, Department must exist, Salary non-negative, Join Date valid) enforced server-side (EmployeeValidator) and mirrored client-side (RHF+Zod), field-level errors surfaced in the UI. Delete requires AlertDialog confirmation. UpdatedAt server-only by construction. 12 backend integration tests + 4 frontend RTL/MSW tests, all green. Code-reviewed (Standards+Spec); fixed 2 duplication smells, added missing Join Date validation+test, and caught/fixed a critical locale bug (DateOnly.Parse used current-culture Buddhist calendar on th-TH, corrupting dates — now InvariantCulture+ParseExact). Verified live end-to-end (create/edit/delete) in a browser.

title: Infra Repo — Compose Orchestration
description:
## What to build

The `infra` repo: a `docker-compose.yml` (no application source code) that pulls the backend and frontend images published to GHCR by their respective CI pipelines, plus a PostgreSQL service, and brings the full stack up together with a single `docker-compose up`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `docker-compose.yml` references the backend and frontend images by their GHCR tags (not a local build context)
- [ ] Includes a PostgreSQL service and wires the backend to it via the existing provider config
- [ ] `docker-compose up` brings up backend + frontend + Postgres such that the app is reachable and usable end to end in a browser
- [ ] README in the `infra` repo documents the one command needed to bring the whole stack up locally

## Blocked by

9 — Multi-Database Verification (PostgreSQL via Docker)

title: CI Pipelines — Backend & Frontend
description:
## What to build

Independent CI pipelines for the backend and frontend repos. Each pipeline builds the app, runs its test suite, and — only on a green run — builds and pushes a Docker image to GitHub Container Registry (GHCR).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Backend repo's workflow runs `dotnet build` + unit + integration tests on every push/PR
- [ ] Backend workflow builds and pushes a Docker image to GHCR only when the build/test step is green
- [ ] Frontend repo's workflow runs the build + component test suite on every push/PR
- [ ] Frontend workflow builds and pushes a Docker image to GHCR only when the build/test step is green
- [ ] A deliberately broken test in either repo causes the image-push step to be skipped, not just the build to fail silently

title: Multi-Database Verification — PostgreSQL via Docker
description:
## What to build

Verification that the connection-provider abstraction built in the walking skeleton actually works against PostgreSQL, not just SQLite: run Postgres via Docker, point the backend at it via the existing config switch, and confirm migrations and core CRUD work unchanged. This is a hardening/verification slice, not a new feature.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A Postgres container can be started locally (e.g. via `docker run` or a compose snippet scoped to this ticket)
- [ ] Setting the existing provider config to Postgres and pointing at that container applies all EF Core migrations cleanly, with no code changes required
- [ ] A basic CRUD smoke check (create + read an Employee) passes against the Postgres-backed instance
- [ ] Any Postgres-specific migration or mapping issue found is fixed so both providers stay green

## Blocked by

1 — Walking Skeleton
notes: Heads up from rzy's code review: the InitialCreate migration was generated while Sqlite was the active provider, so it bakes in Sqlite-specific column type strings ("INTEGER", "TEXT") and a "Sqlite:Autoincrement" annotation on Employees/Departments. This migration will NOT apply cleanly as-is against Postgres. EF Core's documented fix is to generate a second, Postgres-flavored migration (temporarily point Database:Provider at Postgres and rerun 'dotnet ef migrations add') — EF tags each migration with its ActiveProvider and Database.Migrate() only applies the set matching the currently configured provider. Note decimal(18,2) on Employee.Salary is fine as-is (Postgres treats decimal as a numeric alias), so no change needed there.
close_reason:
Verified against a live Postgres 17 container (docker run --name excel-management-postgres -e POSTGRES_USER=excelmgmt -e POSTGRES_PASSWORD=excelmgmt_dev_only -e POSTGRES_DB=excel_management -p 5432:5432 postgres:17-alpine). Found and fixed two real Postgres-specific issues:
1. The Sqlite-scaffolded InitialCreate/AddUsers migrations create tables that "work" on Postgres (TEXT/INTEGER are valid Postgres type names) but with wrong semantics (no auto-increment, boolean columns stored as INTEGER) - added a new PostgresInitialCreate migration retyping columns to native Postgres types (varchar/boolean/date/timestamptz + identity columns), with explicit USING casts for the four conversions Postgres won't do implicitly (TEXT->timestamptz, TEXT->date, INTEGER->boolean x2).
2. That new migration only applies when Postgres is the active provider (migrationBuilder.ActiveProvider guard) since Sqlite shares the same migration history and already has the right shape - Sqlite doesn't understand the raw ALTER...TYPE...USING SQL. Also had to suppress EF Core's PendingModelChangesWarning in AppDbContext.OnConfiguring since the two providers intentionally end up with different column-type models.
Full CRUD (login, create, read, filter) smoke-tested end to end against a fresh Postgres DB; 47/47 backend tests still green on the default Sqlite path. Container stopped/removed after verification.

title: Refresh token rotation lacks server-side revocation
description:
excel-management-1sb implemented JWT refresh as fully stateless: /auth/refresh validates the incoming refresh-token JWT via signature+expiry only (JwtTokenService.ValidateRefreshToken), then issues a brand new access+refresh token pair. There is no server-side store marking the previous refresh token as consumed/revoked, so the "old" refresh token remains fully valid (same signing key, same claims, unexpired) even after a rotation — an attacker who captured a refresh token before rotation can still use it. This satisfies the literal acceptance criterion ("rotates the access token using a valid refresh token") but under-delivers the security intent of token rotation (replay/theft protection), per the code-review Spec-axis finding on excel-management-1sb.

Remediation: add a RefreshTokens table (id/token-hash, user id, expires-at, revoked-at) checked on every /auth/refresh call; mark the presented token revoked and reject any refresh attempt using an already-revoked or unknown token. Alternatively, shorten the refresh token lifetime significantly and accept the reduced protection as a documented tradeoff.

This is an interview take-home exercise; deliberately deferred rather than blocking excel-management-1sb, consistent with how excel-management-ujs.1 was filed for the Department name-uniqueness race.
close_reason: Added server-side RefreshTokens table (id, SHA256 token-hash, user id FK, issued/expires-at, nullable revoked-at) checked on every /auth/refresh call. Login and refresh both insert a row for the freshly-minted refresh JWT; refresh now atomically revokes the presented token's row (rejecting unknown/already-revoked/expired-per-DB tokens with 401) before issuing a new pair -- true rotation, a captured pre-rotation token no longer works. Logout also revokes the current refresh token's row. Root-cause fix along the way: JWTs previously had no jti/nonce, so two tokens minted for the same user within the same second-precision exp window were byte-identical, colliding against the new TokenHash unique index -- added a jti claim to every minted token. Migration scaffolded against a real Postgres 17 (Docker), verified to apply cleanly to a fresh Postgres DB via ef database update, and to Sqlite (the test provider) via the full integration suite. Full backend suite: 64/64 green (62 baseline + 2 new: replay-of-rotated-token rejected, and post-logout reuse rejected). No frontend changes needed.

title: Department name uniqueness: handle race between check and save
description: Code review on excel-management-9n4 found: Department create/update validates name uniqueness via a check-then-act query (IDepartmentRepository.NameExistsAsync) before saving, while Department.Name also has a DB-level unique index (AppDbContext). Under concurrent requests creating/renaming to the same name, the check can pass for both requests before either commits, and the loser's SaveChangesAsync throws an unhandled DbUpdateException (500) instead of the friendly ValidationProblem. Low practical risk (single-admin tool) but worth catching DbUpdateException for a unique-constraint violation and converting it to the same Name validation error.
close_reason: Program.cs: wrapped Department create/update endpoint bodies in try/catch(DbUpdateException), converting the DB unique-index violation into the same ValidationProblem the check-then-act NameExistsAsync path already returns, instead of an unhandled 500. Added a deterministic regression test (fake IDepartmentRepository throwing DbUpdateException from CreateAsync) rather than a real concurrent-HTTP-requests test — the latter is unreliable against this test factory's shared in-memory SQLite connection, which throws an unrelated 'nested transactions' error under genuine concurrent SaveChangesAsync calls (a test-harness artifact from the shared :memory: connection, not a production concern, since real deployments use pooled/separate connections per request).
